items.title: Trump Trilateral Summit In China, House Democratic Leadership, Anthropic IPO
items.summary: President Trump met with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin together for the first time, but the meeting produced no major breakthrough as tensions remain over Ukraine, technology and Taiwan. House Democrats nominated Hakeem Jeffries to become the next Speaker and are already laying the groundwork for investigations into President Trump’s inner circle as they prepare to take control of the chamber. Anthropic begins trading publicly after the biggest IPO in history, testing how much appetite investors still have for artificial intelligence amid growing concerns about an AI bubble.
items.body: President Trump met with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin together for the first time, but the meeting produced no major breakthrough as tensions remain over Ukraine, technology and Taiwan.

items.title: Trump-Xi-Putin Meeting, Nvidia Board Rejects Haung's Return, Computer System Outages
items.summary: President Trump meets Xi Jinping in China as the two countries remain locked in disputes over trade, rare earths and advanced technology, before Vladimir Putin joins them for a three-way summit aimed partly at projecting global leadership. Nvidia's board says Jensen Huang will not return as CEO, even as the company posts another huge quarter and its interim leadership tries to reassure investors that the chipmaker can stay on top without its founder. Apple, the National Security Agency, the FAA and major banks have all suffered recent computer outages, raising questions about why so many critical systems are breaking down at once.

items.title: Russia-bound ship attacked in Gulf of Finland
items.summary: Finnish defence forces say that Ukraine was likely behind the drone attack on the vessel.
items.body: A Russian cargo vessel bound for the country's Baltic exclave Kaliningrad has been hit by a drone attack in the eastern Gulf of Finland, Russian and Finnish authorities say. The ship - the Sparta II - caught on fire after the strike on Saturday morning, before drifting into Finnish waters. Finnish defence forces said Ukraine was likely behind the attack.

items.title: Denmark accuses Russia of plotting to assassinate US-Ukrainian rapper
items.summary: The Russian embassy in Denmark has denied the allegation, which has led to Russia's defence attaché being expelled.
items.body: Denmark has accused Russian intelligence services of plotting to assassinate a Ukrainian-American near Copenhagen, saying they had "planned" and "initiated" the attempt. Denmark's security and intelligence agency (PET) said it had stopped individuals who were intending to kill the person, named by Danish media as rapper Kyivstoner, at a concert in September.

items.title: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
items.summary: Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years. Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.

items.title: Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked
items.summary: The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia. The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who said they had been moved without the necessary permissions.

items.title: Now get out of that! How can the new James Bond film get around 007’s death in No Time to Die?
items.summary: Was it all a dream? Has Bond been in hiding? Or will Robert Pattinson simply report to HR on his first day? Russell T Davies, David Hare and more give their takes “James Bond will return,” says the closing title on No Time to Die, the most recent James Bond film and the final one to star Daniel Craig. It is just as well: Bond has to all appearances been vaporised by sea-launched missiles, having been infected by nanobots programmed to attack his nearest and dearest at the slightest touch. No one would believe that one of the world’s most successful film series would come to such an abrupt halt, but no doubt a little reassurance helped. Nevertheless, the first order of business for scriptwriter Steven Knight and director Denis Villeneuve will be dealing with it: how to revive and re-energise a character at the heart of the action. Speculation on their best way forward has been rife, and previous examples are not hard to find. Sherlock Holmes was killed off by Arthur Conan Doyle by fighting his arch enemy Professor Moriarty at the Reichenbach Falls in the story The Final Problem, only to resuscitate him a decade later with The Adventure of the Empty House. Superman is apparently killed at the end of Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice, but resurrected in Justice League for the fight against Steppenwolf. Arguably the most enduring pop-culture return is Bobby Ewing’s famous shower scene in the TV show Dallas in 1986, which attempted to ensure continuity by suggesting Ewing’s death was his wife’s dream. And even Ian Fleming toyed with killing off Bond, with a climactic poison scene at the end of his 1957 novel From Russia with Love, and leaving him amnesiac and vulnerable to Soviet attack at the finish of You Only Live Twice, the last Bond novel published in Fleming’s lifetime.

items.title: Spacecraft reaches Mercury on second-ever mission to enter its orbit
items.summary: BepiColombo double probe will map planet’s surface and study its interior to shed light on its unusually large core After a voyage of more than eight years and 6bn miles, a joint European-Japanese space mission has arrived at Mercury and is preparing to swing into orbit around the tiny, barely explored world. The BepiColombo mission will become only the second in history to circle the first rock from the sun and the smallest planet in the solar system when flight controllers fire the spacecraft’s thrusters on Saturday and send it into orbit.

items.title: £10m ‘once-in-a-generation’ study to explore effects of children’s social media ban
items.summary: Research to look at whether ban can make meaningful change in mental health and wellbeing for under-16s Countries around the world are considering social media bans for children, but whether this would work in practice has been hotly debated. Now researchers are seeking answers through a major scientific study led by Wellcome, which will be the first of its kind. Ten research projects will explore topics ranging from children’s mental health to their sleep and physical activity, comparing factors before and after the social media ban for children under 16 is introduced in the UK in spring 2027.

items.body: A heterotroph (Greek heteros = another and trophe = nutrition) is an organism that requires organic substrates to get its carbon for growth and development. == In food chains == A heterotroph is known as a consumer in the food chain. Consumers are organisms that cannot make their own food supply. They use the food that producers make, or they eat other organisms. Animals are consumers. To stay alive, consumers must get food from other organisms. There are three types of consumers:Herbivores, Carnivores, and Omnivores. === Herbivores === Consumers that only eat plants are called herbivores. The word herbivore comes from the Latin words herba, which means "grass or herb," and vorare, which means "to eat." A giraffe is an example of a herbivorous consumer. === Carnivores === Consumers that only eat animals are called carnivores. The word comes from the Latin carnis, which means "flesh", and vorare, which means "to eat." A tiger is an example of a carnivorous consumer. === Omnivores === Consumers that eat both plants and animals are called omnivores. The word comes from the Latin omnis, which means "all" and vorare. Humans are a good example of an omnivorous consumer. == Related pages == Autotroph Mixotroph == References ==

items.title: Tellurium(II) chloride
items.summary: Tellurium(II) chloride, also known as tellurium dichloride, is a chemical compound. Its chemical formula is TeCl2. It contains tellurium in its +2 oxidation state. It also contains chloride ions. == Properties == Tellurium(II) chloride is a black solid. It absorbs water. It can be oxidized to tellurium(IV) chloride. items.title: Juan Carlos: From people's king to Spain's pariah
items.summary: At just ten years old, Juan Carlos was handed over to General Franco as a hostage – the price his father paid to keep their family's claim to the Spanish throne alive. It was the start of an apprenticeship designed to produce Franco's ideal successor: a king who would keep the dictatorship's ideals alive long after its architect was gone. However, as Paul Preston tells Danny Bird, Juan Carlos would go on to confound expectations by overseeing Spain’s transition to democracy – only to face disgrace in more recent years. ----- GO BEYOND THE PODCAST Explore the history of Spain before the reign of Juan Carlos in this episode on Franco: https://bit.ly/4bc61UL ----- GET MORE WITH MEMBERSHIP Become a HistoryExtra podcast member and unlock access to The Full Story podcast, plus enjoy ad-free listening, early access to other podcast episodes, and a member-exclusive newsletter.
